reading.body:
Tecnodati S.R.L. is an OpenStreetMap point tagged as a data center with zero megawatts recorded, no operator, no website, and no confirmation that it operates computing equipment.

The record is a name, a coordinate in Italy, and a tag. Its only source is an OpenStreetMap tagging review. The name combines the Italian word for data with the standard Italian limited-liability suffix, which the accompanying note treats as plausible for a small IT or data-services business. Plausible is not verified, and the note says so directly.

For AI capacity accounting, a facility with no megawatt figure cannot be added to any estimate of compute supply or power demand. The point sits 18.6 miles from Parma Airport, which locates it but says nothing about electrical service, cooling, or whether servers are present. The zero is a missing measurement, not a measured zero.

What the data cannot answer is the question a reader would actually ask. It cannot say whether a company called Tecnodati exists, whether it runs racks, or how much power it draws. The research note states that confirmation stopped when search quota ran out, so the missing operator website reflects a missing search rather than a confirmed absence. Other Italian entries in the same source carry names unrelated to computing, including an accounting firm, a foam manufacturer, and an auto-club branch, which makes an on-theme name weak evidence on its own.
